record.paper_title: Some open problems in computational algebraic geometry
record.context_brief: Inclusions among loci up to genus 48
record.original_question: For every genus g <= 48, determine the inclusion relations among the automorphism-group and signature loci of genus-g algebraic curves in the moduli space M_g.

evidence.quote: In the above diagram are given inclusions among the loci of genus 4 curves.
Problem 5. Determine the inclusions among the loci for all g <= 48

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{M}_g$ denote the coarse moduli space of smooth complex projective algebraic curves of genus $g\geq 2$. For a finite group $G$ and a signature $s=(g_0;m_1,\dots,m_r)$ (consisting of a non-negative integer $g_0$ and integers $m_i\geq 2$), define the locus
$$\mathcal{M}_g(G,s)\subseteq\mathcal{M}_g$$
to be the set of isomorphism classes of smooth genus-$g$ curves $C$ such that $G$ embeds in $\mathrm{Aut}(C)$ and the quotient map $C\to C/G$ has genus $g_0$ and branching data $(m_1,\dots,m_r)$. For each $g_0$ and signature $s$, by classical Riemann–Hurwitz / Fuchsian-group considerations, these loci are irreducible (or have known components) and have dimension depending only on $s$. Together with the loci $\mathcal{M}_g(G)$ where the full automorphism group equals $G$, these are called the automorphism-group and signature loci.

Problem: For every integer $g$ with $2\leq g\leq 48$, enumerate all signature–group pairs $(G,s)$ for which $\mathcal{M}_g(G,s)$ is non-empty, and determine completely the inclusion relations
$$\mathcal{M}_g(G',s')\subseteq\mathcal{M}_g(G,s)$$
among all such loci inside $\mathcal{M}_g$ (equivalently, produce the Hasse diagram of these loci under inclusion).
artifact.category_tag: Automorphism loci of algebraic curves in M_g
artifact.status_search_result: Breuer's GAP-based classification provides, for each g ≤ 48, the complete list of signature–group pairs occurring in genus g, and follow-up work (Magaard, Shaska, and collaborators) has eliminated pairs that do not give full automorphism groups and has worked out inclusion diagrams in low genus (notably g = 2, 3, 4). However, a complete, uniformly verified Hasse diagram of inclusions among all such loci for every g up to 48 has not been published; only partial determinations exist in the literature.

status_evidence.title: The locus of curves with prescribed automorphism group (Magaard et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: For each g ≤ 48, Breuer produced a list containing all signature-group pairs in genus g.
status_evidence.claim: Enumeration of signature-group pairs up to g=48 is known (Breuer).

status_evidence.title: On automorphisms of algebraic curves (Contemporary Mathematics)
status_evidence.snippet: Part II was written in order to eliminate those signature-group pairs that do not yield the full automorphism group of a curve.
status_evidence.claim: Refinement to full automorphism groups is ongoing; inclusion relations partially known.

status_evidence.title: arXiv:math/0205314 - The locus of curves with prescribed automorphism group
status_evidence.snippet: Restricting the action to a subgroup H of G yields an inclusion of loci; dimension depends only on signature.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical framework for inclusions exists, but full diagram for all g ≤ 48 not completed.
